episodes.212072: An upper level disturbance moving across the central Rockies combined with higher moisture across the southeast plains of NM resulted in the development of multiple severe thunderstorms across southern Roosevelt County during the mid afternoon to mid evening hours. These thunderstorms resulted in three rounds of hail up to ping pong diameter between Pep and the Roosevelt and Lea County border. Back building of severe thunderstorms across this area resulted in some minor flooding in culverts and low lying areas. Thunderstorms tapered off just before sunset on May 21st due to the loss of daytime heating. Two more rounds of thunderstorms developed across the northeast and east central plains of NM during the afternoon on May 22nd and 23rd. These storms resulted in a severe wind gust at a public weather station near Melrose on May 22nd and at Tucumcari Municipal Airport on May 23rd. Storms exited into west Texas during the evening hours. The Trigg wildfire was also discovered in far eastern San Miguel County, burning through May 25th before coming under control.
episodes.212123: An widespread area of showers and thunderstorms produced heavy rainfall of 2-4 inches in a short period of time during the morning that resulted in flash flooding and some downed trees in Cullman county. Isolated strong storms occurred in the afternoon hours as well. One storm downed a tree in Morgan county, Alabama.
episodes.212128: Daytime heating combined with mid level moisture under an upper high over New Mexico resulted in high based showers and storms across the higher terrain and nearby lower elevations across central New Mexico during the afternoon and early evening hours on May 24th. One decaying thunderstorm resulted in a severe wind gust at Raton Crews Municipal Airport.
episodes.212273: A shortwave in the southwesterly flow aloft allowed thunderstorms to develop during the afternoon of the 23rd. Storms developed first off the higher terrain and spread northeastward into the Permian Basin of west Texas. A few storms managed to produce large hail, along with some flash flooding.
episodes.212353: Scattered storms developed late Sunday afternoon near the Yellow Medicine - Chippewa County line and strengthened as they moved east towards Sibley and McLeod Counties. There were a few isolated reports of severe wind and hail during this time. The storms reached peak intensity as they turned south and moved through southern Sibley, Nicollet, and eastern Brown Counties. ||The largest hail reports of the evening were half dollar size in Sibley County, and the strongest wind was observed in Nicollet County (estimated 60 mph) where large amounts of dirt and dust were lofted just ahead of the storm along the gust front. It is rare to see this phenomenon occur in Minnesota, but several weeks of below normal precipitation meant many fields were dry and primed for dirt to be blown.
episodes.212503: A stationary front stalled along the Ohio Valley region, sparking showers and thunderstorms. Some storms produced heavy rainfall, which resulted in flooding.
episodes.212668: Thunderstorms again developed late in the afternoon of the 23rd in two separate locations. Isolated thunderstorms initially developed across the western South Plains into the Permian Basin which produced large hail. Numerous outflow boundaries interacted with each other creating new convection and several landspout tornadoes. A second area of thunderstorms moved into the southern Texas Panhandle from eastern New Mexico. Both areas of thunderstorm activity merged into a single complex of thunderstorms producing severe wind gusts as it moved across the Rolling Plains through the late evening hours.
episodes.212793: A stalled frontal boundary north of the region, as well as Gulf Coast and Atlantic Coast sea breezes, combined with usual early summer high instability and PWATs close to 2 inches to produce numerous showers and thunderstorms across the region, as well as isolated severe downbursts.  Slow storm motion attributed to localized heavy rainfall and minor flooding.
episodes.212891: A warm front was lifted into the area by a passing low on the 23rd of May, then the front stalled over central West Virginia and southwest Virginia through the 24th. Another low eventually pushed the boundary northward and then steered a cold front west to east across the area on the 25th.||Rounds of rain and thunderstorms traversed the area, with most robust activity occurring in the afternoon and evening of the 23rd and 24th. The majority of the area received one to three inches of rain during this time, with a few pockets between three and four inches.  Excessive rainfall flooded roads in Gilmer, Harrison, Lewis, Raleigh, Taylor, and Upshur Counties and led to a mud slide in Kanawha County. A couple of severe thunderstorms also produced damaging winds which downed trees and power lines in Logan and Mingo counties the evening of the 24th.
episodes.212892: A warm front was lifted into the area by a passing low on the 23rd of May, then the front stalled over central West Virginia and southwest Virginia through the 24th. Another low eventually pushed the boundary northward and then steered a cold front west to east across the area on the 25th.||Rounds of rain and thunderstorms traversed southeast Ohio, with most robust activity occurring  in the afternoon and evening hours of the 23rd and 24th. Much of southeast Ohio received one to two and a half inches of rain during this time, along with pockets of three to four and a half inch accumulations. Excessive rainfall flooded roads in Athens, Jackson, Perry, Morgan, Gallia, Meigs, and Lawrence counties and led to minor flooding on portions of Sunday Creek, Duck Creek, and the Little Muskingum.
episodes.213023: A stalled frontal boundary north of the region, as well as Gulf Coast and Atlantic Coast sea breezes, combined with usual early summer high instability and PWATs close to 2 inches to produce numerous showers and thunderstorms across the region, as well as isolated severe downbursts. Slow storm motion attributed to localized heavy rainfall and minor flooding.
episodes.213030: A lingering stalled front remained in the forecast area 5/23, but a embedded shortwave in the general troughing pattern moved in during the afternoon and evening hours, leading to scattered convection to develop. The environment ahead of this shortwave was characterized by MLCAPE values over 2000 J/kg and effective shear near 30-35 kts. Scattered strong to severe storms moved across the forecast area during the afternoon and evening hours, bringing damaging winds, hail up to golf ball sized, and even a report of a waterspout over Lake Murray in SC.
episodes.213031: A fairly typical summertime pulse environment took shape the afternoon and evening of 5/24 with PWAT's between 1.80-2.0 and MLCAPE values over 1500 J/kg. This led to scattered convective development across the forecast area, but with weak mean 800-300mb flow, storm motions were under 10-15kts. As a result, strong thunderstorms persisted over Sardis GA for nearly 2 hours with efficient rain rates, causing flash flooding south of Sardis.
episodes.213062: A passing shortwave generated showers and thunderstorms across the upper Ohio Valley in the evening of the 24th. Some training of the storms resulted in higher amounts approaching 3 inches, which resulted in some isolated flash flooding in Ohio, West Virginia, and western Pennsylvania.
episodes.213063: A passing shortwave generated showers and thunderstorms across the upper Ohio Valley in the evening of the 24th. Some training of the storms resulted in higher amounts approaching 3 inches, which resulted in some isolated flash flooding in Ohio, West Virginia, and western Pennsylvania.
episodes.213064: A passing shortwave generated showers and thunderstorms across the upper Ohio Valley in the evening of the 24th. Some training of the storms resulted in higher amounts approaching 3 inches, which resulted in some isolated flash flooding in Ohio, West Virginia, and western Pennsylvania.
episodes.213210: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed on a daily basis across the region over Memorial Day weekend as a result of several passing upper level disturbances. Some storms produced severe hail, damaging winds, and flash flooding. Significant flash flooding occurred in North Richland Hills in Tarrant County on May 25th.
episodes.213244: A warm front was lifted into the area by a passing low on the 23rd of May, then the front stalled over central West Virginia and southwest Virginia through the 24th. Another low eventually pushed the boundary northward and then steered a cold front west to east across the area on the 25th.||Rounds of rain and thunderstorms traversed southeast Ohio, with most robust activity occurring in the afternoon and evening hours of the 23rd and 24th. The majority of northeast Kentucky received one to three inches of rain during this time. Excessive rainfall led to some flooded roads in Greenup County.
episodes.213317: Severe thunderstorms occurred across the Texas Panhandle from during the late afternoon through late evening hours on May 22nd through May 24th. On the 22nd the environment was such that a few isolated storms were able to produce hail between one inch and 2.75 inches across parts of the southern Texas Panhandle. On the 23rd, thunderstorms produced straight line winds in excess of 58 mph across the central to northern Texas Panhandle. Additional severe wind gusts also occurred on the 24th. Several landspouts also occurred during this time period. An additional landspout also occurred on May 26th in the southwest Texas Panhandle.
episodes.213333: A midlevel shortwave lifted north through East Tennessee on May 24th, producing widespread showers and thunderstorms. Repeated bouts of heavy rain affected Knox and Loudon counties, producing some flash flooding in the South Knoxville and Loudon areas respectively. Additionally, a severe thunderstorm occurred in Hamilton County.
episodes.213374: An organized line of thunderstorms and consolidated outflow swept from the Texas Rolling Plains into southwestern Oklahoma early on the morning of the 24th. This activity produced several observations of strong to severe wind gusts.
episodes.213385: A stationary front stalled across the Ohio Valley region during the morning, eventually lifting north in the evening hours. Showers and thunderstorms developed along this boundary with locally heavy rainfall.
episodes.213570: Clusters of showers and thunderstorms affected the area for multiple days ahead of a cold front. Some storms were severe with impacts to trees and power lines.
episodes.213594: A developing thunderstorm over Tampa Bay produced a brief EF-0 tornado that affected the Villages of Bayport community in Hillsborough County.  Elsewhere, easterly sea breeze afternoon convection produced a funnel cloud near Buckingham in Lee County.
episodes.213627: Storms moved through SE Texas and produced strong winds and heavy rainfall.
episodes.213830: A mesoscale convective system developed from storms in south Texas and moved across the northwestern Gulf into coastal Louisiana. As this complex reached the coastal waters south of Mississippi, severe marine wind gusts occurred.
episodes.213969: The dynamic breakup front finally arrived at the lower reaches of the Yukon River across the Yukon Delta by late May 2026. This resulted in severe, cascading flood impacts for multiple communities as the high water made it's way to the mouth of the Yukon River, inundating the coastal delta.
episodes.214033: A low pressure system slowly moved east across northern Ohio during the evening on May 24, 2026. Showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of a trailing cold front, and a brief but intense thunderstorm impacted the Mansfield area with rainfall rates of 3 to 4 inches per hour.
episodes.214141: A southwest mid- and upper-level flow pattern of modest strength was in place across the Ohio Valley on May 24th. Ample moisture was present across central Kentucky, with precipitable water values of 1.7 to 1.8 inches observed during the late morning and early afternoon hours. Scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms moved across Kentucky during this time period, with narrow corridors of heavy rainfall amounts occurring across portions of the Bluegrass region where multiple lines of storms moved through. The most significant of these heavy rainfall swaths led to flash flooding across portions of Nicholas County, where multiple low water crossings and roads near small streams were submerged by sudden rises in water levels.
episodes.214279: A subtle shortwave moved across Wyoming and brought isolated showers and thunderstorms. With very dry air at the surface, a few thunderstorms produced strong wind when they collapsed. Wind gusts of 58 mph or more occurred in Natrona, Lincoln and Sweetwater Counties, with the strongest gust of 66 mph at Mount Coffin in the Salt and Wyoming Range.
episodes.214404: A weak wave in northwest flow aloft enhanced the low-level jet into southeast South Dakota with moisture and better deep-layer shear arriving by late day near a weak frontal boundary.  With mixed-layer instability from 1500-2200 J/kg and marginally supportive deep layer shear of 40-45 kts, isolated supercells developed with mainly hail from stronger cells up to 2 inches in diameter.

The Emmonak High School had to be opened as an emergency shelter for displaced residents.
